review_notes: Read the whole target file and grepped the repo for uses of factorRadiusLevel and factorSwitchList. The factorSwitchList lemmas are membership/forall lemmas with no simp-normal-form concern. The only simp-interface problem I found is that factorRadiusLevel, an if-chain on Fin 3, has no evaluation lemmas, so every downstream use unfolds the definition ad hoc. I did not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed lemmas make the existing proofs shorter.

findings.excerpt: if k = 0 then u₀ else if k = 1 then (u₀+u₂)/2 else u₂
findings.problem: The definition is an if-chain on `k : Fin 3`, but it has no evaluation lemmas for the three concrete levels, such as `factorRadiusLevel u₀ u₂ 0 = u₀`, `... 1 = (u₀+u₂)/2` and `... 2 = u₂`. Every use that needs a concrete level unfolds the definition and relies on `norm_num`/`simp` to decide `(2 : Fin 3) = 0`. This happens in this file (`factorRadiusLevel_nonneg`, `factorRadiusLevel_monotone`, `actual_phase_switch_clock` all use `fin_cases k <;> norm_num [factorRadiusLevel]`) and in other files: MultipointCompletionExhaustion has `norm_num [factorRadiusLevel]` to prove `factorRadiusLevel (u₀ i) (u₂ i) 2 = u₂ i`, and MultipointActualBudget uses `simpa only [ρ, actualFactorStops, factorRadiusLevel, Fin.reduceEq, ite_false, cutoffStop]`. The simp interface is the raw `if` expression, so the proofs are brittle and expose the implementation.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma factorRadiusLevel_zero (u₀ u₂ : ℝ) : factorRadiusLevel u₀ u₂ 0 = u₀`, `@[simp] lemma factorRadiusLevel_one ... 1 = (u₀+u₂)/2` and `@[simp] lemma factorRadiusLevel_two ... 2 = u₂`. Each should be proved by `simp [factorRadiusLevel]` or `rfl`/`decide`-style reduction. Then replace the ad hoc `norm_num [factorRadiusLevel]` and `simp only [..., factorRadiusLevel, Fin.reduceEq, ite_false]` calls with `simp` or `fin_cases k <;> simp`. The `actual_phase_switch_clock` statement could also use a small helper or lemma instead of repeating the same if-chain.
findings.benefit: Concrete levels normalise to `u₀`, `(u₀+u₂)/2` and `u₂` without unfolding the definition. The `fin_cases ... norm_num [factorRadiusLevel]` and `Fin.reduceEq`/`ite_false` boilerplate shrinks, and downstream proofs such as MultipointCompletionExhaustion and MultipointActualBudget no longer depend on how the definition is written.
